newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen warns against split in party.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen warns against split in party.

text.p: Cambodian leader Hun Sen on Tuesday threatened to resign from his powerful political party if its membership did not follow him.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who is the vice president of the Cambodian People's Party (CPP), warned the party would collapse without him.

"I will ... walk away from the party if all of you don't follow (me) and if I walk out from the Cambodian People's Party, all of you will fall backward because you need (support) from Hun Sen," he said in a speech broadcast on state radio.
Hun Sen's comments appeared to be aimed at heading off any potential rifts in his ex-communist CPP.

Hun Sen overthrew First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6 after two days of fighting in Phnom Penh, and his forces are now closing in on the remnants of the prince's army in the northwest.
Hun Sen has justified his actions by accusing Ranariddh of smuggling weapons and bringing Khmer Rouge guerrillas into Phnom Penh.
Analysts said the political violence has been unpopular with more moderate elements within the CPP and suggested there may be dissent within the party.
Hun Sen's comments may have been a warning to any disgruntled party members, they said.
Hun Sen, who ruled Cambodia with coalition partner Ranariddh before the coup, also said he was committed to working not only on behalf of his party but for all Cambodians.
"I do not act only for the benefit of the party and then let others die," Hun Sen said.
Foreign Minister Ung Huot has been appointed to replace Ranariddh and Hun Sen has said the move shows his commitment to maintaining Cambodia's coalition government.
On Tuesday Hun Sen also reiterated his commitment to free and fair elections in 1998.
